lessons.title: Discussing the work of family members
lessons.objective: Take part in a discussion about family occupations, waiting for one’s turn and listening to others.
lessons.course:
In a discussion, each person speaks in turn. We listen when others speak, we do not interrupt, and we can agree or disagree politely: “I agree with Ngum because…”, “I think differently: …”.
Family occupations: farmer, trader, teacher, nurse, mechanic, driver, carpenter, civil servant.
lessons.model: In a group, Tabi says: “My mother is a nurse. She helps sick people.” Manka answers: “I agree that nurses are important, because they save lives.”
lessons.guided: In a group of three, each person presents the work of a family member. Then discuss: which job would you like to do, and why?
lessons.answer: We say: I think differently, because…
accept: We say: I think differently, because…
lessons.remediation: Use a talking object: only the person holding it speaks.
lessons.transfer: Ask a family member about his or her work and report it to the class.

practice.prompt: Which rule is good for a discussion?
practice.explanation: We listen and speak in turns.

practice.prompt: Match each worker with his or her work.
practice.answer: mechanic: cars; trader: goods; nurse: sick people.

practice.prompt: Listen and say what the speaker thinks.
practice.listen: I agree with Tabi, because farmers feed the whole country.
practice.answer: The speaker agrees that farmers are important because they feed the country.

lessons.title: Reading numbers from 101 to 500 in words
lessons.objective: Read numbers from 101 to 500 written in words and match them with figures.
lessons.course:
We read numbers in hundreds, tens and units. 245 is two hundred and forty-five. 308 is three hundred and eight. 460 is four hundred and sixty.
In British English we say “and” after the hundreds.

support.title: Read aloud
support.text:
125 one hundred and twenty-five
300 three hundred
407 four hundred and seven
500 five hundred

lessons.model: A tailor’s receipt says “three hundred and fifty francs”. The adult reads it and writes 350.
lessons.guided: Match number cards in words and in figures. Read each pair aloud.
lessons.exercise: Write in figures: two hundred and nine.
lessons.remediation: Read hundreds only first (100, 200, 300), then add tens and units.
lessons.transfer: Read prices written in words on receipts or in a newspaper.
lessons.materials: Number cards in figures and in words.

practice.prompt: Write in figures: four hundred and seventy-three.
Match the words with the figures.
practice.explanation: Read hundreds, then tens and units.

practice.prompt: Which one is “two hundred and fifty”?

lessons.title: Writing numbers from 101 to 500 in words
lessons.objective: Write numbers from 101 to 500 in words correctly.
lessons.course:
To write a number in words: write the hundreds (three hundred), then “and”, then the tens and units with a hyphen (forty-two): 342 → three hundred and forty-two.
Careful with spelling: forty (not fourty), eight, eleven, twelve, fifteen.
lessons.model: The adult writes a cheque-like note: “Pay four hundred and fifteen francs (415 frs) to the carpenter.”
lessons.guided: Write five numbers in words. Check the spelling of forty, fifteen and twelve.
lessons.remediation: Write the hundreds word first, then add the rest.
lessons.transfer: Write the price of three things at the market in words.

practice.prompt: Write 325 in words.
Which spelling is correct?
Complete.

lessons.title: Helping verbs and continuous tenses
lessons.objective: Use helping verbs (am, is, are, was, were, will be) to form the present, past and future continuous.
lessons.course:
A helping verb helps the main verb. Continuous tenses show an action in progress: helping verb + verb-ing.
Present continuous: I am working. She is selling. They are building.
Past continuous: He was driving. We were sewing.
Future continuous: She will be teaching.
lessons.model: The adult describes a picture of a building site: “The mason is building a wall. The carpenters are making the roof. Yesterday, they were carrying blocks.”
lessons.guided: Describe what each worker in a picture is doing now, then what he was doing yesterday at the same time.
lessons.exercise: Complete: The tailor ___ sewing a dress now.
accept: The tailor is sewing a dress now
lessons.remediation: Practise the present continuous with I am, then with he / she is.
lessons.transfer: Say what three people at home are doing right now.

practice.prompt: Complete with am, is or are.
practice.text: I [[am]] reading. The farmers [[are]] planting. Mama [[is]] cooking.
practice.explanation: am with I, is with one person, are with many.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is in the past continuous?
Complete: Tomorrow at 8 a.m., the teacher ___ teaching.
accept: Tomorrow at 8 a.m., the teacher will be teaching

lessons.title: Multiplying and multiples
lessons.objective: Multiply using the tables up to 10 and find multiples of a number.
lessons.course:
Multiplying is adding equal groups: 4 groups of 6 = 4 × 6 = 24.
The multiples of 5 are the numbers in the table of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25… A number times 10 gets a zero at the end: 23 × 10 = 230.
lessons.model: A tailor sews 6 shirts a day. In 5 days: 5 × 6 = 30 shirts.
lessons.guided: Say the tables of 6 and 7. Find the first five multiples of 4.
lessons.exercise: A carpenter makes 8 chairs a week. How many in 6 weeks?
lessons.remediation: Use arrays of dots to see the groups.
lessons.transfer: Find a situation of equal groups at home (plates, eggs in a tray).

practice.prompt: Which number is a multiple of 6?
Complete the multiples of 4.

lessons.title: Sharing and grouping: division with remainders
lessons.objective: Divide by sharing or grouping, with and without a remainder, and check with multiplication.
lessons.course:
Division shares equally or makes equal groups. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 because 5 × 6 = 30.
Sometimes something is left over: 23 ÷ 4 = 5 remainder 3, because 4 × 5 = 20 and 3 are left.
We share fairly: each person gets the same.
lessons.model: A baker shares 27 loaves among 4 shops: each shop gets 6 and 3 loaves remain.
lessons.guided: Share counters into equal groups. Write the division and the remainder, then check.
lessons.remediation: Use counters and share one by one.
lessons.transfer: Share sweets equally among friends and say the remainder.

practice.prompt: 29 ÷ 4 gives 7 remainder …?
How do we check a division?
choices: multiply the answer by the divisor and add the remainder
practice.answer: multiply the answer by the divisor and add the remainder

lessons.title: Capacity: l, dl, cl and ml
lessons.objective: Measure and compare capacities using l, dl, cl and ml, and convert between them.
lessons.course:
Capacity is how much a container can hold. 1 l = 10 dl = 100 cl = 1 000 ml.
A bottle of oil: 1 l. A glass: 25 cl. A spoon of medicine: 5 ml.
lessons.model: The palm oil seller fills bottles of 1 l. Four glasses of 25 cl make 1 l.
lessons.guided: Fill a 1 l bottle with glasses or cups and count. Read the capacity labels of containers at home.
lessons.exercise: How many ml are in 1 l?
lessons.remediation: Compare containers by pouring water from one to another.
lessons.transfer: Read the capacity on three bottles at home.

practice.prompt: 2 l = ? cl
How many glasses of 25 cl fill a 1 l bottle?
Which unit for a spoon of medicine?
practice.explanation: A spoon holds a few millilitres.

lessons.title: Mass: grams and kilograms
lessons.objective: Weigh objects and compare masses using g and kg.
lessons.course:
Mass tells how heavy something is. 1 kg = 1 000 g. A bag of rice: 5 kg. A tin of tomato paste: 70 g.
At the market, sellers use scales. We read the scale to know the mass.
lessons.model: The seller puts beans on the scale: 2 kg. Half a kilogram is 500 g.
lessons.guided: Compare objects by holding them, then weigh them with a kitchen scale. Order them from lightest to heaviest.
lessons.exercise: How many grams are in 1 kg?
lessons.remediation: Compare two objects by holding them first.
lessons.transfer: Read the mass on packets of food at home.

practice.prompt: 3 kg = ? g
Which is heavier?
Half a kilogram is how many grams?

lessons.title: Tools, machines and building a house
lessons.objective: Identify tools and machines of local trades and the main materials and steps of building a house.
lessons.course:
Each trade has tools: farming (hoe, cutlass, wheelbarrow), carpentry (saw, plane, hammer), tailoring (sewing machine, scissors), bricklaying (trowel, spirit level), fishing (net, hook, canoe).
To build a house: choose the site, dig the foundation, lay blocks or bricks, put the roof, then doors, windows and plastering. Materials: sand, cement, gravel, blocks, wood, iron rods, roofing sheets.
lessons.model: The adult describes a building site: “The mason lays the blocks with a trowel and checks with a spirit level that the wall is straight.”
lessons.guided: Make a list of tools you can see in your quarter and the trade of each. Put the steps of building a house in order.
lessons.exercise: Which tool checks that a wall is straight?
lessons.remediation: Match three tools with three trades first.
lessons.transfer: Visit a building site with an adult (from a safe distance) and name three materials.
lessons.materials: Pictures of tools and building sites.

practice.prompt: Put the steps of building a house in order.
practice.answer: foundation, blocks, roof, doors and windows.
practice.explanation: We build from the ground up.

practice.prompt: Match each tool with its trade.
practice.answer: trowel: bricklaying; plane: carpentry; net: fishing.

practice.prompt: Which material do we mix with sand and water to make mortar?
practice.explanation: Cement, sand and water make mortar.

lessons.title: Les métiers : on coupe l’herbe avec une machette
lessons.objective: Nommer des métiers et dire avec quel outil on travaille.
lessons.course:
Des métiers : le cultivateur, le commerçant, le forgeron, le couturier, le pêcheur, le menuisier.
Pour dire l’outil : « On coupe l’herbe avec une machette. » « Le couturier coud avec une machine à coudre. » « Le pêcheur attrape les poissons avec un filet. »

support.title: Mots utiles
support.text:
le cultivateur — la houe, la machette
le couturier — la machine à coudre
le pêcheur — le filet

lessons.model: L’adulte mime : « Je suis cultivateur. Je laboure avec une houe. »
lessons.guided: Mime un métier ; ton partenaire devine et dit l’outil avec « avec ».
lessons.exercise: Avec quoi le pêcheur attrape-t-il les poissons ?
lessons.remediation: Travaille trois métiers avec des images.
lessons.transfer: Dis en français le métier d’une personne de ta famille.

practice.prompt: Relie le métier et l’outil.
practice.answer: cultivateur : houe ; couturier : machine à coudre ; menuisier : scie.

practice.prompt: Complète.
Qui vend au marché ?

lessons.title: How people earn a living: farming, trading, fishing
lessons.objective: Describe the main economic activities of the locality and their importance.
lessons.course:
Farming: people grow food crops (maize, cassava, plantain, beans) and cash crops (cocoa, coffee, tea, cotton), and rear animals (poultry, pigs, cattle).
Trading: people buy and sell in markets and shops.
Fishing: people catch fish in the sea, rivers and lakes.
These activities feed the population and bring money to families and to the country.
lessons.model: The adult explains: “In the West region, many farmers grow coffee. In Limbe, many people fish.”
lessons.guided: Interview a family member about his or her work. Sort activities into farming, trading and fishing.
lessons.exercise: Is cocoa a food crop or a cash crop?
lessons.remediation: Use pictures of crops and activities.
lessons.transfer: At the market, find three products of farming and one of fishing.
lessons.materials: Pictures of crops, markets and fishing.

practice.prompt: Match each product with its activity.
practice.answer: coffee: farming; fish: fishing; buying and selling: trading.

practice.prompt: Which is a food crop?
Why are these activities important?
practice.answer: They feed people and bring money.
practice.explanation: They feed the population and bring income.

lessons.title: The toolbox of five craftsmen
lessons.objective: Identify the tools of the moulder, carpenter, weaver, sculptor and painter, and use simple tools safely.
lessons.course:
The moulder uses clay, water and a board. The carpenter uses a saw, a hammer, a plane and sandpaper. The weaver uses raffia, a frame and a needle. The sculptor uses a chisel, a mallet and wood. The painter uses brushes, paints and a palette.
Craftsmen keep their tools clean, sharp and in a box.
lessons.model: The adult opens a toolbox and names each tool and its craftsman.
lessons.guided: Sort pictures of tools into the five toolboxes. Sand a small piece of wood with sandpaper.
lessons.exercise: Which craftsman uses a chisel and a mallet?
lessons.remediation: Start with the carpenter and the painter.
lessons.transfer: Visit a craftsman with an adult and ask about his tools.
lessons.materials: Pictures of tools; sandpaper and wood.

practice.prompt: Match each tool with its craftsman.
practice.answer: brush: painter; raffia: weaver; plane: carpenter.

practice.prompt: What does sandpaper do?
Why do craftsmen keep tools in a box?
practice.answer: To keep them safe and find them easily.

lessons.title: Photography: recording events
lessons.objective: Identify devices used in photography and take photos respectfully to record an event.
lessons.course:
We take photos with a camera, a mobile phone or a tablet. Photos record events: a birthday, a school day, a harvest.
A good photo: the light comes from behind the photographer, the person or object is in the middle, we hold the device still. We always ask permission before taking a photo of someone.
lessons.model: The adult takes a photo of a plant: the sun is behind, the plant is in the middle, the phone is still.
lessons.guided: With an adult’s device, take three photos of an event at home (with permission). Choose the best one and say why.
lessons.exercise: What do we do before taking a photo of someone?
lessons.remediation: Practise holding the device still with both hands.
lessons.transfer: Make a small photo record of a family event with an adult.
lessons.materials: A camera or phone (with an adult).

practice.prompt: Which device can take photos?
Where should the light be for a good photo?
choices: behind the person in the photo
practice.explanation: The light must fall on the subject.

practice.prompt: Draw the photo you would take of your school.
practice.answer: A drawing framed like a photo.
practice.explanation: Put the main subject in the middle.

lessons.title: Long jump and rope jumping
lessons.objective: Jump with a run-up, take off on one foot and land safely; jump rope in rhythm.
lessons.course:
Long jump: run up, take off on one foot, swing the arms forward, land on both feet in the sand and bend the knees.
Rope jumping: turn the rope, jump with both feet together, keep a regular rhythm.
lessons.model: The adult runs, takes off from a line and lands in sand with bent knees.
lessons.guided: Do five long jumps; a partner measures with steps. Jump rope ten times without stopping.
lessons.exercise: How do we land in long jump?
lessons.answer: On both feet with bent knees.
accept: on both feet with bent knees
On both feet with bent knees
lessons.remediation: Jump from standing before adding the run-up.
lessons.transfer: Play rope jumping with friends and count together.
lessons.materials: A sand pit or soft ground, a rope.

practice.prompt: Put the long jump in order.
practice.explanation: These are the phases of the long jump.

practice.prompt: Bih jumps 2 m, then 3 m. How many metres in all?

lessons.title: Polite requests and responses in the family language
lessons.objective: Use polite requests and responses, speak in turns and listen attentively in the family language.
lessons.course:
Every language has polite forms: to greet, to ask, to thank, to apologise, to answer an elder. In many cultures, we lower the voice, use a title (uncle, mama, papa) or bow slightly to show respect.
We listen attentively and do not interrupt.
lessons.model: The adult shows how to ask an elder for water politely in the family language, and how to thank him.
lessons.guided: With an adult, learn three polite forms in the family language: please, thank you, sorry. Use them during a role play.
lessons.exercise: What do we do when an elder is speaking?
lessons.answer: We listen and do not interrupt.
accept: we listen and do not interrupt
We listen and do not interrupt
lessons.remediation: Practise one polite form at a time.
lessons.transfer: Use the polite forms with your elders all week.
lessons.materials: An adult who speaks the language.

practice.prompt: Match the situation with the polite form.
practice.answer: gift: thank you; asking: please; mistake: sorry.
practice.explanation: Say them in the family language with an adult.

practice.prompt: Which behaviour is polite?
practice.explanation: We speak one at a time.

practice.prompt: Say “thank you” in the family language to someone at home.
practice.answer: Thank you said in the family language.

lessons.title: Computers at school, at the hospital and at the bank
lessons.objective: Explain the uses of computers in school and in society and use them responsibly.
lessons.course:
At school, computers keep pupils’ marks, type examinations and help to learn. At the hospital they keep patients’ records. At the bank and the market they count money and print receipts. At home, they help to communicate.
We use computers responsibly: we ask permission, we do not break settings, we do not stay too long in front of the screen.
lessons.model: The adult tells how the school secretary uses a computer to print report cards.
lessons.guided: Make a poster: “Where are computers used?” with four places and one use for each.
lessons.exercise: Name one use of a computer at school.
lessons.answer: For example: typing examinations or keeping marks.
lessons.remediation: Think of one place first: the school office.
lessons.transfer: Ask a worker in your town how he or she uses a computer.

practice.prompt: Match each place with a use of computers.
practice.answer: hospital: records; bank: money; school: examinations.

practice.prompt: Which behaviour is responsible?
choices: ask permission before using a computer
practice.answer: ask permission before using a computer

practice.prompt: Write two uses of computers in your town.
